transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, doctor. I came in because... well, since my wife’s fall, things have just completely derailed. 

I’ve always been the man with the lists and the plan, you know? But lately, I just sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I find myself crying, or snapping over absolutely nothing. And everything else is just piling up—the bills, my mentoring calls, even just basic housework. It’s like I just can’t make myself function anymore.
Since your wife’s fall, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I wouldn't say I've lost interest, exactly. It's more that... I just don't have the energy or the focus for them right now. Like my mentoring calls, I still care about the young men I work with, I just... I can't bring myself to pick up the phone. My mind is just so consumed with my wife and her care, there's no room for anything else.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been going on for about two months now. Basically, ever since she had that fall... that's when everything at home just completely changed.
Since your wife’s fall, have you been feeling persistently anxious or excessively worried?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious. I mean... I'm concerned for her recovery, obviously, but it's not this constant worry or panic about what might happen next. 

It's more just... being completely overwhelmed by the day-to-day reality of it right now. I don't really feel nervous or on edge in that way. I just feel incredibly heavy and stuck.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself or that you would be better off dead?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or... or wanting to die. As hard and exhausting as this all is right now, I don't feel that way at all. I just want us to get through it.
How has your sleep been since your wife’s fall?

My sleep has been alright, actually. I mean, I'm tired all the time from everything that's going on, but once I get to bed, I usually sleep through the night. I haven't noticed any real problems with falling asleep or waking up too early. It's just the waking hours that are so exhausting.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since your wife’s fall?

No, my appetite hasn't really changed. I mean... I'm still eating my regular meals. I might just be throwing together simpler things right now because I'm so drained, but I haven't lost my appetite or anything like that. I'm eating fine.
